history.period: Contemporaneous with the Sun Temple complex (11th century) - detailed dating unverified
history.summary: A small chariot-shaped Shiva shrine inside the Modhera Sun Temple complex, opposite the Guda Mandapa and Sabha Mandapa - the only living temple in the complex. The main Shiva linga is surrounded by five smaller lingas, hence 'Panchlinga'. Local accounts hold that Allauddin Khilji's raiders destroyed the main Sun idol but missed this smaller shrine, so daily puja by a resident priest has continued ever since; the roof and some walls were later restored. The Solanki kings were Suryavanshi by clan but Shaivite by religion, so a Shiva shrine within the Sun complex is consistent with its origins. No dedicated historical study of this shrine was found - its 11th-century dating is inferred from the complex and should be verified (verify). name: Panchlinga Shiva Temple
town_description: Modhera is a village in Mehsana district of north Gujarat on the Pushpavati river. Said to have been the original settlement of the Modha Brahmins, it is steeped in legend - the Skanda Purana places Rama's yajna here in the forest of Dharmaranya. The village is dominated by the 11th-century Sun Temple complex, now an ASI monument and the venue of the annual Modhera Dance Festival.

travel.road: Inside the Modhera Sun Temple complex; same access as the Sun Temple, ~24 km south of Patan
